title: Transcendental Methods As A Dictionary
notes: Open by framing Appendix B as a controlled dictionary, not as permission to forget algebra. Over C, algebraic equations can be read holomorphically, but the return trip requires named hypotheses. Point to the notebook path and page span so the audience knows this deck is tied to the assigned appendix.

title: Local Analytic Spaces From Equations
notes: Make the local construction feel concrete. A finitely generated C-algebra presented by equations gives a common zero set with holomorphic functions, and the structure sheaf is obtained by quotienting holomorphic germs. Stress that nilpotents and gluing are still present; analytic does not mean set-theoretic simplification.

title: The Analytification Functor
notes: Use the notebook ladder as the first artifact anchor, even though the slide supplies the clean labels. The key teaching move is functoriality: X, sheaves, and morphisms all have analytic shadows. The warning is equally important: a functor gives maps, not automatic equivalences of categories.

title: Basic Dictionary Entries
notes: Treat this as a dictionary page with two columns. Some entries are nearly topological or local once the construction is made, while cohomology needs comparison maps and hypotheses. The alpha_i arrows should be heard as questions first, and as isomorphisms only after GAGA supplies the setting.

title: Five Comparison Questions
notes: Separate the five comparison questions before stating the theorem. Students often remember GAGA as one large equivalence, but the appendix distinguishes objects, uniqueness, sheaves, sheaf uniqueness, and cohomology. The board and ledger make projective or proper hypotheses visible as the switch that changes not automatic into preserved.

title: GAGA In The Projective Case
notes: State GAGA as a projective theorem and then give the proof pipeline at the level of strategy. Projective space cohomology is computed first, resolutions transfer the result to coherent sheaves, and closed subvarieties inherit the comparison. Repeat that projectivity is doing real work here.

title: Chow's Projective Algebraization
notes: Present Chow's theorem as a reverse direction in projective space. A compact analytic subset may begin life as holomorphic geometry, but inside complex projective space compactness and analytic structure force algebraic equations. The drawing is intentionally original: it illustrates algebraization without copying any source figure.

title: Compact Complex Manifolds
notes: Use this taxonomy slide to slow down vocabulary. Compact, analytic, algebraic, projective, and Moishezon are not synonyms in higher dimension. The inequality for the field of meromorphic functions gives a numerical test, and dimension one is flagged as special rather than representative of all dimensions.

title: Finite Covers And Riemann Existence
notes: Connect Riemann existence to finite covers as a categorical comparison, not only a theorem name. For normal finite-type X over C, a normal finite analytic cover of X^h is represented by a finite algebraic morphism over X under analytification. This is the doorway from complex topology to the algebraic fundamental group.

title: Moishezon Failure Modes
notes: The failure-mode slide prevents a common overreach: many meromorphic functions alone do not hand you projective algebraic geometry without the correct extra structure. Keep the schematic abstract on purpose. It marks where Moishezon data, compactness, Kahler geometry, and projectivity can diverge.

title: Kahler Metrics And Hodge Classes
notes: Move from algebraic comparison to differential input. A Kahler metric is a closed positive (1,1)-form, and an integral Hodge class adds arithmetic topology to the picture. Use the notebook chart as evidence of the implication map, while the form motif names the hypotheses students should inspect.

title: Algebraicity Criteria Map
notes: Read the criteria map as a hypothesis map, not as a proof of Kodaira or Moishezon. Hodge data can force projectivity, Moishezon plus Kahler can also force projectivity, and projective algebraic manifolds provide Kahler metrics. The arrows remember assumptions, not vague resemblance.

title: The Exponential Sequence
notes: Make the exponential sequence feel operational. Additive holomorphic functions are exponentiated into invertible holomorphic functions, and integer shifts are exactly the kernel. Once this short exact sequence is sent to cohomology, line bundles and Chern classes appear as measurable defects of choosing logarithms.

title: Picard, Neron-Severi, Chern Class
notes: Use the Picard slide to gather the cohomological consequences into one place. The checks from the notebook certify the toy exponential identities and a positive Hermitian form, while the formulas identify Picard, Picard zero, Neron-Severi, and the first Chern bridge. Keep the emphasis on connections.

title: Curve Case And Winding Lab
notes: Close with the curve case and the lab. For curves, Picard zero becomes a complex torus quotient, and the winding picture lets students predict why z and z plus an integer exponentiate to the same value. The linked lab is the hands-on check for that collapse.
